skill.name: nano-banana-edit
skill.description: Edit images with Google Nano Banana 2 (image-to-image edit endpoint) on RunComfy. Documents Nano Banana Edit's strengths (preserve subject identity, swap background, localize edits with spatial language, multi-image batch edits up to 20 inputs), the schema, and when to route to GPT Image 2 edit / Flux Kontext / Nano Banana 2 t2i instead. Calls `runcomfy run google/nano-banana-2/edit` through the local RunComfy CLI. Triggers on "nano banana edit", "edit with nano banana", "image edit nano banana", or any explicit ask to edit with this model.
skill.summary: Edit single images or batches with Nano Banana 2 through RunComfy while controlling preservation, framing, resolution, and output format.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most flags are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and a documented token path. The skill still recommends unpinned package execution and sends prompts and image references to RunComfy. Its shell examples do not adequately protect generated user text from shell quoting failures.

remediation.issue: Generated prompt JSON can cross a shell boundary inside a single-quoted argument.
remediation.suggestion: Invoke the CLI with an argument array and a JSON serializer, or use a protected input file. Never interpolate user text into a shell command.

remediation.issue: The installation commands execute unpinned npm packages with global or remote effects.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions, publish integrity information, and require user confirmation before package installation.

remediation.issue: Prompts and image references are transmitted to a third-party model service.
remediation.suggestion: Require user consent, link the service privacy and retention terms, and warn against sending confidential images or expiring signed URLs.

content.value_statement: Image edits often change subjects, framing, or branding unintentionally. This skill structures Nano Banana 2 requests for focused edits, consistent batches, and controlled outputs through RunComfy.
actual_capabilities: Edits one to twenty image URLs in a single RunComfy request.
Preserves specified subject, pose, clothing, branding, framing, or lighting details.
Targets backgrounds, objects, labels, and spatial regions with direct instructions.
Controls output count, seed, aspect ratio, resolution, format, and safety tolerance.
Downloads completed PNG, JPEG, or WebP results to a selected output directory.
limitations: Inputs must be publicly fetchable HTTPS URLs rather than local image paths.
Each request accepts at most twenty inputs and produces at most four outputs.
Long compound edits can drift and may require separate passes.
Multilingual text replacement may work better with another image editing model.

use_cases.title: Standardize product galleries
use_cases.description: Apply one background and framing treatment across multiple product images while preserving each product.

use_cases.title: Create campaign variants
use_cases.description: Generate controlled background, clothing, or label variations for visual review and testing.

use_cases.title: Automate image revisions
use_cases.description: Run repeatable image edits with fixed dimensions, formats, seeds, and output locations.

prompt_templates.title: Replace a background
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit {image_url}. Keep the subject, pose, and clothing unchanged. Replace only the background with {background_description}. Save the result to {output_directory}.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs one focused background change.

prompt_templates.title: Change one object
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit {image_url}. Preserve {protected_details}. Change only {target_region} to {requested_change}. Keep all other pixels as consistent as possible.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs a localized object or label edit.

prompt_templates.title: Process a consistent batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit all images from {image_urls}. Preserve {protected_features}. Apply {change} consistently. Lock the aspect ratio to {aspect_ratio} and resolution to {resolution}.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs matching edits across a product or portrait series.

prompt_templates.title: Generate controlled variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit {image_urls} with {change}. Preserve {protected_features}. Use seed {seed}, {aspect_ratio}, {resolution}, and {format}. Produce {count} variants with web search {web_search_setting}.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs reproducible variants with explicit output controls.

output_examples.input: Keep the portrait subject unchanged and replace only the office background with a bright studio wall.
output_examples.output: One edited portrait with the original subject and pose, a bright studio wall, and the requested file format.

output_examples.input: Apply the same neutral background, square framing, and resolution to three product images.
output: Three edited product images with matching backgrounds.
Consistent square framing and resolution across the batch.
Downloaded files stored in the selected output directory.

output_examples.input: Remove only the leftmost object from a still life while preserving the table and lighting.
output_examples.output: An edited still life without the leftmost object, while the remaining objects, table, and lighting stay consistent.

best_practices: State preservation requirements before describing the requested change.
Use precise spatial terms and split complex edits into separate passes.
Lock aspect ratio, resolution, prompt structure, and seed when comparing batch variants.
anti_patterns: Do not combine many unrelated changes in one instruction.
Do not omit the features that must remain unchanged.
Do not send confidential images or URLs without reviewing RunComfy data handling terms.

faq.question: Does this skill edit local files directly?
faq.answer: No. Inputs must use publicly fetchable HTTPS URLs, and the CLI downloads generated outputs to the selected directory.

faq.question: How many images can one request process?
faq.answer: One request accepts one to twenty input images and can produce one to four output images.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint supports PNG, JPEG, and WebP output.

faq.question: Can it preserve a person's identity?
faq.answer: It is designed for identity preservation, but results can drift. State every protected feature before the requested change.

faq.question: Where are prompts and images processed?
faq.answer: RunComfy receives the prompt, and its model server fetches the supplied image URLs for processing.

faq.question: Is a RunComfy account required?
faq.answer: Yes. Interactive use requires RunComfy login, while automated environments can provide a RunComfy token.
